testing_status: on hold until the user gives the testing go-ahead

comparison.adoption_gate: At least 5 percent median complete-task improvement on the chosen workload, or useful capacity gain with an explicitly accepted speed tradeoff; no unexplained quality failure or new swap. Report control drift and all raw passes.
comparison.percentage_rules: TPS gain = 100*(candidate/control-1). Time reduction = 100*(1-candidate/control). Requires finite positive matched metrics. Do not add percentages from separate experiments.

experiments.title: Measure real expert reuse
experiments.implementation: Diagnostic entry point and capture/parser staged; native CPU self-test passes. No model or GPU run yet.
experiments.hypothesis: Four/five verification tokens may reuse enough selected experts to justify sparse matrix work.
experiments.only_change: Install a read-only evaluation callback for ten expert IDs per token; preserve weight bytes and all launchers.
proof: Matched greedy text and token IDs including warmups
All 48 main expert layers captured
Ten distinct IDs per token in 0..511
2048-byte routing row stride
Target/helper roles separate
Zero new swap
experiments.limits: Callbacks split/synchronize graphs. Exclude their timing from TPS history. A high reuse rate alone does not prove a fast kernel.

experiments.title: Locate the remaining GPU work
experiments.implementation: Split callback, buffer attribution and parser staged; real GPU behavior untested.
experiments.hypothesis: Shared matrices, attention/state or other operations account for the gap left by isolated matrix timings.
experiments.only_change: Deliberately split scheduled computational nodes into diagnostic intervals; never enable this in app launchers.
proof: Matched greedy text/token output
CPU monotonic boundaries assign every computational GPU buffer once
Main/helper and prompt/generation separated
No additional math op in an isolated interval
Explicit instrumentation overhead versus fresh control
Zero new swap
stop_if: Callback event cap or excessive logs
experiments.limits: Splitting removes fusion and adds synchronization/command-buffer overhead. Costs rank diagnostic paths, not original kernel time or accelerator occupancy.

experiments.title: Try more useful context
experiments.implementation: Protocol and fixture design prepared. Native context setting exists; long-context harness and quality checks still require implementation/validation.
experiments.hypothesis: 8K context may fit with useful headroom and allow larger documents without unacceptable latency or quality loss.
experiments.only_change: Context capacity 4096 to 8192. Keep F16 cache, engine, helper depth and workers fixed.
prerequisites: Memory budget derived from actual allocation logs
proof: ABBA timing on identical 512/2048-token inputs and 128-token outputs
Separate 6144-token retrieval fixture at 8K with room for output
Facts at beginning/middle/end and distractors; verify exact answers
Target/helper KV, recurrent state, QSA and scratch allocations logged separately
Zero new swap
experiments.limits: Higher configured capacity is not proof of long-input quality. The 6144-token case has no 4K TPS comparison. A separate quantized-cache trial may follow; do not combine it with this test.

experiments.title: Overlap bounded SSD lookup reads
experiments.implementation: Design template only. No prefetch code or candidate build exists.
experiments.hypothesis: If model-specific lazy-row waits are material, bounded asynchronous page advice may hide part of them.
experiments.only_change: Add macOS handling for already-known lazy lookup rows; preserve shard bytes and mmap/lazy behavior.
prerequisites: Isolated engine manifest and real implementation
proof: Exact output/data parity
Bounds, alignment, shard lifetime, duplicate-row and failure-path checks
Bounded resident pages and outstanding work
Matched warm-request ABBA timing
Label cold observations separately; no system cache purge
Zero new swap
stop_if: No repeatable complete-task gain after two narrow approaches
experiments.limits: System-wide disk reads cannot establish lookup wait. The 96 MiB cap is a proposed bound, not an implemented cache or established optimum.

experiments.title: Optimize one measured GPU operation
experiments.implementation: Design template only; target family is intentionally unset until diagnostic evidence is available.
experiments.hypothesis: One demonstrated expensive shape can use less dequantization/memory work or better cooperative matrix input.
experiments.only_change: One dispatch/kernel in an isolated engine, keeping GGUF bytes and fallback behavior.
prerequisites: Actual candidate patch, manifest and build receipt
proof: CPU-reference math, odd/aligned shapes and inactive-expert cases
Actual dispatch proof
Original controls preserved
Fresh ABBA model comparisons and semantic checks
Matched TPS, first-token and full-reply percentages
Zero new swap
stop_if: Two narrow approaches repeatedly under 2-3 percent
experiments.limits: A synthetic kernel win is not a model TPS win. Do not force a sparse few-row workload into MMA merely because the hardware supports matrix acceleration.

experiments.title: Explore larger-model capacity
experiments.implementation: Feasibility template only; pager, precision upgrade and larger model downloads are absent.
experiments.hypothesis: A bounded expert residency map could trade SSD traffic and speed for larger or higher-precision weights.
experiments.only_change: Expert residency/paging policy in a separate prototype after a complete capacity budget.
prerequisites: User-selected capacity goal and acceptable minimum speed
Testing go-ahead before downloads or model runs
proof: Mapping, eviction, in-flight references and fallback correctness
Prefill and verification miss handling
Read bytes/latency and resident-set peak
Zero OS swap growth
Actual quality/precision benefit and sustained response speed
stop_if: Memory accounting depends on OS swap
Minimum useful speed cannot be met
experiments.limits: Capacity may improve while TPS falls. Mac unified memory does not pool with another PC. This plan does not allocate, download or page model weights.
